column2: Right now, every rider pays a fare to get on the bus or the train.
column3: Today, nobody pays a fare to ride the bus or the train.

column2: Right now, roads are paid for by a tax on gas, and drivers of electric cars pay almost nothing toward them.
column3: Today, drivers pay for the roads by the mile they drive, not by the gallon they buy.

column2: Right now, whole neighborhoods can only get internet from one company, at whatever price it sets.
column3: Today, a public network brings internet to homes the companies passed by.

column2: Right now, nearly all of our road money goes to highways, and the buses get what's left.
column3: Today, part of our highway money goes to buses and trains.

column2: Right now, a worker can earn too much to get Medicaid and still too little to buy insurance.
column3: Today, working people who earn too little to buy insurance can get Medicaid.

column2: Right now, a grown adult who can work can get Medicaid without working.
column3: Today, an adult who can work has to work, train or volunteer to keep Medicaid.

column2: Right now, cash assistance doesn't ask anything of the adults who can work.
column3: Today, an adult who can work has to look for work to get cash assistance.

column2: Right now, Medicare pays whatever the drug companies ask for most medicines.
column3: Today, Medicare bargains with the drug companies over what it pays.

column2: Right now, preschool is something a family pays for or does without.
column3: Today, every four-year-old can go to preschool.

column2: Right now, a family that picks a private school pays for it twice, in tuition and in taxes.
column3: Today, public money follows a child to a private school.

column2: Right now, a starting teacher can earn less than a manager at the store down the road.
column3: Today, the law sets a floor under what a teacher is paid.

column2: Right now, a young person can leave school owing more than their parents paid for a house.
column3: Today, much of what students borrowed has been forgiven.

column2: Right now, there is no tax on what people earn here.
column3: Today, people here pay a tax on what they earn.

column2: Right now, a family's property tax can climb as fast as the assessor says.
column3: Today, the law limits how fast property taxes can rise.

column2: Right now, a family pays sales tax on every loaf of bread and gallon of milk.
column3: Today, groceries carry no sales tax.

column2: Right now, a cook and a company owner pay the same income tax rate.
column3: Today, higher incomes pay a higher rate.

column2: Right now, nothing stops the budget from spending more than comes in.
column3: Today, the law says the budget has to balance every year.

column2: Right now, the pension fund can be shorted whenever the budget gets tight.
column3: Today, the law says the pension fund gets its full payment on schedule.

column2: Right now, nothing makes us keep money aside for a bad year.
column3: Today, the law makes us keep money aside for a bad year.

column2: Right now, the debt limit can be raised without cutting a dollar of spending to match.
column3: Today, any rise in the debt limit has to come with spending cuts to match.

column2: Right now, most of our land is zoned so that nothing but a single house can go up on it.
column3: Today, apartments can be built in neighborhoods that once allowed only single houses.

column2: Right now, a new apartment building can go up without a single unit a working family can afford.
column3: Today, new buildings have to set aside units a working family can afford.

column2: Right now, a landlord can raise the rent as much as they like when the lease runs out.
column3: Today, the law limits how much the rent can go up each year.

column2: Right now, most tenants face an eviction in court without a lawyer.
column3: Today, a tenant facing eviction gets a lawyer.

column2: Right now, most families who qualify for housing help sit on a waiting list for years.
column3: Today, every family that qualifies gets a housing voucher.

column2: Right now, the federal minimum wage has not gone up in years, while everything else has.
column3: Today, the federal minimum wage is higher than it was.

column2: Right now, a city can't set a minimum wage of its own.
column3: Today, a city can set its own minimum wage.

column2: Right now, someone working full time at the minimum wage still can't cover rent.
column3: Today, the minimum wage is higher than it was.

column2: Right now, a worker who stays home with a new baby or a sick parent can lose a paycheck.
column3: Today, a worker can take paid leave for a new baby or a sick parent.

column2: Right now, public workers can't bargain together over their pay.
column3: Today, public workers can bargain together over their pay.

column2: Right now, a state job application asks about a criminal record before anything else.
column3: Today, a state job application doesn't ask about a criminal record up front.

column2: Right now, a worker in a union shop can be made to pay union dues.
column3: Today, no worker can be made to pay union dues to keep a job.

column2: Right now, selling cannabis is a crime, and the money goes to the black market.
column3: Today, cannabis is sold legally, in licensed stores.

column2: Right now, a payday lender can charge hundreds of percent a year on a small loan.
column3: Today, the law caps the interest on a consumer loan.

column2: Right now, new buildings are still hooked up to gas.
column3: Today, new buildings are built without gas hookups.

column2: Right now, a family buys its power from one utility and has no other choice.
column3: Today, a family can pick who supplies its electricity.

column2: Right now, utilities can burn whatever is cheapest to make our power.
column3: Today, utilities have to make a growing share of our power clean.

column2: Right now, a county with dirty air doesn't have to have a plan to clean it.
column3: Today, a county with dirty air has to have a plan to clean it.

column2: Right now, bottles and cans end up on roadsides with nothing to bring them back.
column3: Today, there's a deposit on bottles and cans that brings them back.

column2: Right now, a company can put carbon into the air without paying a cent for it.
column3: Today, a company pays for the carbon it puts into the air.

column2: Right now, power plants can put as much carbon into the air as they like.
column3: Today, power plants are limited in how much carbon they put into the air.

column2: Right now, the police answer only to themselves when a complaint comes in.
column3: Today, a civilian board looks into complaints against the police.

column2: Right now, our police don't work with federal immigration agents.
column3: Today, our police work with federal immigration agents.

column2: Right now, whether someone waits for trial in jail can come down to whether they can pay bail.
column3: Today, nobody sits in jail before trial just because they can't pay bail.

column2: Right now, someone who has served their whole sentence still can't vote.
column3: Today, someone who has served their sentence can vote again.

column2: Right now, a seventeen-year-old can be tried as an adult.
column3: Today, young people stay in juvenile court longer.

column2: Right now, nothing requires a gun to be locked away from children.
column3: Today, the law requires a gun to be stored away from children.

column2: Right now, a person can carry a hidden gun without a permit.
column3: Today, carrying a hidden gun takes a permit.

column2: Right now, an eighteen-year-old can buy a handgun.
column3: Today, a person has to be older to buy a handgun.

column2: Right now, a person attacked outside their home has a duty to retreat if they safely can.
column3: Today, a person attacked anywhere they have a right to be can stand their ground.

column2: Right now, Washington pays most of the cost when a disaster hits a state.
column3: Today, the states pay a larger share of what a disaster costs.

column2: Right now, a judge has to hand down the same long sentence no matter the case.
column3: Today, judges have more room to fit a sentence to the case.

column2: Right now, most voters have to go to a polling place or ask for a ballot by mail.
column3: Today, every voter gets a ballot in the mail.

column2: Right now, a citizen has to sign up to vote before they can.
column3: Today, a citizen is registered to vote automatically.

column2: Right now, the politicians draw their own district lines.
column3: Today, an independent commission draws the district lines.

column2: Right now, a voter doesn't have to show a photo ID at the polls.
column3: Today, a voter shows a photo ID at the polls.

column2: Right now, a citizen who misses the registration deadline can't vote that year.
column3: Today, a citizen can register and vote on the same day.

column2: Right now, an official can leave office on Friday and lobby their old colleagues on Monday.
column3: Today, a former official has to wait before lobbying their old colleagues.

column2: Right now, a town has to ask the state's permission for most of what it wants to do.
column3: Today, towns can do more without asking the state first.

column2: Right now, a legislator can serve for as long as they keep winning.
column3: Today, the law limits how long a legislator can serve.

column2: Right now, a lawmaker in Washington can buy and sell stock in the very companies they write laws for.
column3: Today, lawmakers in Washington can't trade stocks.

column2: Right now, the people who live in the nation's capital pay federal taxes and have no voting member in the House or the Senate.
column3: Today, the nation's capital is a state.

column2: Right now, a person can be turned away from a job or an apartment for who they are.
column3: Today, nobody can be turned away from a job or an apartment for who they are.

column2: Right now, the parks get whatever is left at the end of the budget.
column3: Today, the parks have money set aside for them every year.

column2: Right now, abortion is legal here.
column3: Today, the law restricts abortion here.

column2: Right now, a child can open a social media account in a minute with no one checking their age.
column3: Today, social media sites have to check a user's age.

column2: Right now, government agencies can scan a face in a crowd with no rules at all.
column3: Today, the law limits how government uses facial recognition.

column2: Right now, a company can sell what it knows about you without asking.
column3: Today, a company has to protect what it knows about you.

column2: Right now, there is no national law that protects your personal data.
column3: Today, a national law protects your personal data.

column2: Right now, anyone with a well can pump as much groundwater as they like.
column3: Today, the law limits how much groundwater can be pumped.

column2: Right now, good farmland can be paved over for the next subdivision.
column3: Today, farmland is protected from being paved over.

column2: Right now, the top income tax rate is lower than it was a generation ago.
column3: Today, the top income tax rate is higher than it was.

column2: Right now, there is no national cap on the interest a lender can charge.
column3: Today, a national cap limits the interest on a consumer loan.

column2: Right now, our defense budget is not keeping up with the threats we face.
column3: Today, we spend more on defense than we did.

column2: Right now, foreign aid is less than one penny of every federal dollar.
column3: Today, we give more in foreign aid than we did.

column2: Right now, most goods come into this country with little or no tariff.
column3: Today, goods from abroad carry higher tariffs.

column2: Right now, people wait years, sometimes decades, to come here legally.
column3: Today, more people can come here legally each year.

column2: Right now, full Social Security starts at sixty-seven.
column3: Today, full Social Security starts later than it did.

column2: Right now, a train is not a real choice for most trips in this country.
column3: Today, more of the country can travel by train.

column2: Right now, the biggest farms collect the biggest checks from Washington.
column3: Today, farm subsidies are smaller than they were.
